summary:
Outpost Commander is an interactive, bilingual (English/Spanish) web simulator designed for students ages 7–12 to experience real space mission engineering trade-offs. Players manage a lunar (Shackleton Crater, Artemis) or Martian (Jezero Crater) outpost over 30 days/sols, balancing competing demands across power generation, ECLSS life support, hydroponic food production, regolith radiation shielding, crew morale, and Earth-space communication latency.

Addressing the NASA Space Apps challenge, the game avoids risk-free choices: expanding food or oxygen systems drains power reserves, deploying rovers for science consumes battery power and increases radiation exposure, and Mars missions impose a realistic 14-minute communication delay with Earth. Grounded in curated open data from NASA DONKI, OSDR, Curiosity RAD, and Artemis/LRO, it transforms complex aerospace constraints into engaging, accessible STEM play.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS

Outpost Commander is a browser-based mission control simulator where young learners (ages 7–12) command a 3-person astronaut crew on either the Moon (Shackleton Crater, Artemis program) or Mars (Jezero Crater) across a 30-day/sol mission. Each turn, players allocate limited mission mass and power across four interdependent systems—Solar/Kilopower Energy, ECLSS Life Support, NASA Veggie Hydroponics, and Regolith Radiation Shielding—while managing crew morale, cumulative radiation dose (mSv), rover field expeditions, and narrative Commander Dilemmas.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT

Traditional space STEM materials often oversimplify mission planning or overwhelm kids with heavy jargon. Outpost Commander bridges this gap by letting students learn through cause-and-effect experimentation. Plain-language tooltips explain scientific concepts (such as Sols, Regolith, ECLSS, and Sieverts) in context, while instant English/Spanish switching and a printable personalized Junior Astronaut Certificate make it ready for both home learning and classrooms.

CREATIVITY & DESIGN FACTORS CONSIDERED

- Zero "Free" Choices: Every action carries an authentic engineering trade-off (e.g., boosting life support or hydroponics reduces available power; exploring with the rover yields Science Points at the expense of energy and radiation exposure).

- Real Communication Latency: Selecting the Moon enables near-instant (1.3-second) telemetry assistance from Houston, whereas Mars enforces a realistic ~14-minute one-way signal delay, requiring autonomous decision-making.

- Dynamic Visual & Audio Feedback: An interactive SVG outpost reflects real-time system health, dust storms, and solar flares, paired with synthesized Web Audio cues and unlockable STEM badges.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED

Built using JavaScript (ES6+), React 18, Vite, Tailwind CSS v4, Lucide Icons, native HTML5 SVG animations, and the Web Audio API for procedural sound synthesis.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ACKNOWLEDGMENT

In accordance with NASA Space Apps guidelines, Super Intelligence (generative AI coding and language assistants) was used to assist with React/Tailwind code structuring, procedural Web Audio synthesis logic, and bilingual (English/Spanish) educational copywriting. All game mechanics, NASA dataset curation, and testing were directed and verified by the project creator.
